notes: Starter plant knowledge for Canopy. Replace or extend the 'plants' array with your own data — keep the same field names. Only 'name' is required; any field you leave out is treated as 'not in the plant file yet' by Rootly.

plants.name: Cactus
plants.wateringNotes: Soak thoroughly, then let the soil dry out completely before watering again. Water roughly every 2 weeks in the growing season; cut back to once a month in winter and keep water off the plant during heavy monsoon humidity to avoid rot.
plants.sunlightRule: Needs bright, direct sun. Rotate or reposition the pot weekly so all sides get even light, and give light shade during peak afternoon sun in extreme heat to prevent sunburn.
plants.fertilizerNotes: Feed with a diluted low-nitrogen cactus fertilizer or a thin top-dressing of well-rotted compost every ~2 months in the growing season. No feeding in winter.
plants.lightNotes: Full sun is ideal; a south or west-facing balcony or terrace works well.
plants.humidityNotes: Thrives in dry air (roughly 20–50% RH). Poor air circulation in very humid weather invites fungal rot.
plants.soilNotes: Use a gritty, fast-draining mix (sandy soil + perlite or coarse sand + a little compost). Slightly alkaline to neutral pH is fine. Always use a pot with drainage holes.
careTips: Overwatering is the most common way to lose a cactus — when in doubt, wait.
Use gloves or folded newspaper when repotting.
Wrinkled, soft stems usually mean thirst; mushy, dark stems mean rot.

plants.name: Neem
plants.wateringNotes: Water young plants deeply every 4–6 days. Established neem is drought tolerant and needs far less; avoid waterlogging.
plants.sunlightRule: Full sun. Keep it where it gets at least 6 hours of direct light and rotate the container every couple of weeks for even growth.
plants.fertilizerNotes: Apply well-rotted compost, vermicompost or neem cake roughly every 6 weeks during the growing season.
plants.lightNotes: Loves hot, bright conditions; weak and leggy in low light.
plants.humidityNotes: Tolerates a very wide range from arid to humid, though it grows fastest in warm, moderately humid weather.
plants.soilNotes: Well-drained sandy loam. Tolerates poor and slightly alkaline soils but hates standing water.
careTips: Prune lightly to shape and keep a potted neem to a manageable size.
Leaves can be used to make a mild homemade pest spray for other plants.

plants.name: Rose
plants.wateringNotes: Water deeply at the base every 2 days (daily in peak summer, less in winter). Avoid wetting the leaves — it encourages black spot.
plants.sunlightRule: Give at least 5–6 hours of sun, preferably morning light. Reposition or rotate weekly and provide afternoon shade in the hottest months.
plants.fertilizerNotes: Feed every 2–3 weeks while growing and flowering with vermicompost, well-rotted manure, or a balanced NPK fertilizer; add bone meal to support blooms.
plants.lightNotes: Flowers poorly in shade. Good morning sun with some afternoon relief is the sweet spot.
plants.humidityNotes: Prefers moderate humidity (around 50–70% RH) with good air flow; very humid, still air promotes fungal disease.
plants.soilNotes: Rich, loamy, organic soil with good drainage; slightly acidic to neutral (pH about 6.0–6.8).
careTips: Deadhead spent blooms to encourage more flowers.
Prune dead or crossing stems after the main flowering flush.
Mulch the soil surface to keep roots cool and moist.

plants.name: Tomato
plants.wateringNotes: Keep soil evenly moist — water deeply every day in hot weather (every 2 days in cool weather). Irregular watering can cause blossom-end rot and split fruit.
plants.sunlightRule: Needs 6–8 hours of direct sun. Rotate the pot every few days so all sides ripen evenly, and give light afternoon shade only during extreme heat waves.
plants.fertilizerNotes: Heavy feeder: add compost or vermicompost every 2 weeks, switching to a potash-rich feed once flowers and fruit set.
plants.lightNotes: Fruiting drops sharply with under ~6 hours of sun.
plants.humidityNotes: Does best around 50–70% RH. Very high humidity increases blight and fungal problems.
plants.soilNotes: Rich, loamy, well-drained soil with plenty of organic matter; pH around 6.0–6.8.
careTips: Pinch off side shoots (suckers) on indeterminate varieties.
Water at the soil level, not on the leaves.

plants.name: Tulsi
plants.wateringNotes: Water every 2 days; daily in peak summer and every 3–4 days in winter. Keep the soil moist but never waterlogged.
plants.sunlightRule: Place in 4–6 hours of bright sun, ideally morning sun. Reposition weekly so it doesn't lean toward the light, and provide light shade in intense afternoon heat.
plants.fertilizerNotes: Mix in vermicompost or well-rotted cow-dung manure roughly once a month. Avoid strong chemical fertilizers.
plants.lightNotes: Grows leggy and weak in low light.
plants.humidityNotes: Tolerates a wide humidity range (about 40–80% RH). Sensitive to cold below roughly 10°C.
plants.soilNotes: Loose, well-drained loamy soil rich in organic matter; pH about 6.0–7.5.
careTips: Pinch off flower buds (manjari) to keep the plant bushy and leafy.
Harvest by pinching leaves just above a pair of leaves.
Protect from frost and cold drafts in winter.
